FIG 4Availability by management type

How it is calculated: Available / expected pairs, by management type (diamond); each dot is one facility's own rate.

Who runs the facility, as recorded on the form - government, faith based, or public-private partnership. The diamond is the category's own rate; each hollow dot is one facility in it, with the weakest and strongest named, so a category carried by a few weak facilities can be told apart from one that is low throughout. This is a collected variable, not one derived from the level of care, so the gap between the three is a finding in its own right and not a restatement of the level gradient. Facilities assessed on fewer than 10 medicines are left out of the dots but stay in the diamond.

FIG 5Availability by level of care and drug class

How it is calculated: Count of expected medicines that were on the shelf, split by level of care (left) and drug class (right).

Size - node height and ribbon width - is the count: the 8,381 medicines that were expected at a facility and on the shelf, routed from level of care to drug class. Colour is the level of care, so a ribbon can be traced back to where it starts through the crossings. The availability rate is printed on every node and in every tooltip: the health post node gives the rate across health posts, the antibiotics node the rate across antibiotics, and a ribbon the rate for that level within that class. Colour carries no magnitude here - it says where a flow comes from, not how well that level is stocked. The smallest classes are pooled into one node so the column total still equals the real total.

FIG 6Medicines managed but not on the EML for that level - by level of care

How it is calculated: Molecules a facility manages that the EML does not list at its level / all molecules it manages, by level of care.

Of the 9,017 molecules facilities actually stock, 51 are not authorised at that level of care on the EML. READ THIS BEFORE QUOTING THE FIGURE: 51 of those 51 are medicines whose name could not be matched to the EML list - fixed-dose combinations, test kits, implants and brand names - so their flag is the collector's original answer, never checked against the list. 0 were confirmed against the list. The bar is therefore closer to a measure of how much of the basket the EML list could be matched to than to facilities stocking off-formulary products.

FIG 7Medicines managed but not on the EML for that level - by programme

How it is calculated: Molecules managed but not EML-listed at that level / all molecules managed, by programme. Programmes under 30 left out.

The same measure by vertical programme. ARV, Malaria and FP lead because their products are exactly the ones the name matcher cannot resolve - ARV fixed-dose combinations, malaria RDTs and DHAP, contraceptive implants and IUDs. Essential Medicines and TB are near zero because their products are single molecules that match the list cleanly. The same caveat as FIG 6 applies.

FIG 8Unavailable at the facility - was the stock upstream? By level of care

How it is calculated: Unavailable rows answered 'Yes' at RMS Regional (or Central) / unavailable rows with a Yes or No answer for that store.

FIG 9Regional against Central, by drug class

How it is calculated: Same as FIG 8 - Yes / answered Yes-or-No, per store - by drug class.

Two bars per class, so the tiers are read against each other directly. Where Central is high and Regional low, the stock was in the country but not in the region. Where both are low, the class was short nationally. Classes with fewer than 30 answered rows are omitted; the two denominators differ because a row can carry an answer for one tier and not the other.

FIG 10Regional against Central, by programme

How it is calculated: Same as FIG 8 - Yes / answered Yes-or-No, per store - by programme.

The same pairing by vertical programme. A programme where both bars are short is short at the national store itself.

FIG 11The form's own attribution: distribution issue against nationwide stock-out

How it is calculated: Unavailable rows counted by the form's own distribution_nationwide field: distribution issue vs nationwide stock-out.

distribution_nationwide is a field the instrument itself computes on every unavailable row. It reads "Distribution issue" where the stock existed upstream and "Nationwide stock-out" where it did not, and it agrees with the Regional and Central answers almost exactly - 531 of 545 distribution-issue rows have Central = Yes, and 81 of 87 nationwide rows have Central = No. 184 unavailable rows are left unclassified because no usable upstream answer was given.

FIG 12Attribution by programme

How it is calculated: Rows the form classes 'nationwide stock-out' / unavailable rows it classes either way, by programme.

The share of each programme's unavailable rows that the form classifies as a nationwide stock-out rather than a distribution failure. A tall second column is a procurement problem.

TABLEAll medicines by level of availability

How it is calculated: Per molecule: facilities with it available / facilities expected to hold it - EML-authorised for Essential Medicines, managing it for other programmes.

Every molecule in the basket, least available first. Availability is the share of facilities expected to hold it - EML-authorised for Essential Medicines, managing it for other programmes - that had it on the day of the visit. 1.1Overall tracer medicine availability

Numerator: the facility manages the medicine AND it was on the shelf. Denominator, by medicine_program: for Essential Medicines, every medicine the EML authorises at that level of care - one the facility is supposed to manage but does not counts as unavailable; for every other programme (Malaria, MCCH, FP, ARV, TB, Consumables), only the medicines the facility manages, because programme products are allocated and not holding one is usually policy, not a shortage. 766 of 9,782 pairs (7.8%) are Essential Medicines not managed; 635 more were managed but empty. METHOD 3 - a medicine assessed at more than one strength counts once per facility and is available if ANY strength was on the shelf; 81 items become 71 molecules. 'Unexpired and usable' cannot be applied - no expiry or usability variable is collected, so availability means physically present.

Analysis 2 · Stock adequacy and Inventory accuracy

FIG 2.1Stock adequacy overall

How it is calculated: Months of stock = quantity on hand / average monthly consumption Jun-Aug, on rows in stock with consumption > 0. Under 1 = understock, 1-2 = adequate, over 2 = overstock; each ring is that group / all such rows.

The whole base in one figure: of the 7,900 medicines that were on the shelf with recorded consumption, how much was being held. Only the green ring is the right amount. Stock-outs are not in this figure - adequacy asks how much is held where the medicine is present, and the 816 stock-outs appear in 2.1 instead.

FIG 2.2Stock adequacy mix by level of care

How it is calculated: As FIG 2.1 - months of stock, classed under / adequate / over - shares within each level of care.

Each bar is the full base for that tier, so the segments are the mix rather than the volume - the count is at the right. Stock-outs are not in these bars: adequacy asks how much is held where the medicine is present; stock-outs appear in 2.1 instead. Only the green middle is good news; a group can be weak at either end.

FIG 2.3Stock adequacy mix by programme

How it is calculated: As FIG 2.1 - months of stock, classed under / adequate / over - shares within each programme.

Vertical programmes manage their own ordering, so the mix differs sharply between them.

FIG 2.4Stock adequacy mix by province

How it is calculated: As FIG 2.1 - months of stock, classed under / adequate / over - shares within each province.

Most overstocked province first.

2.1Months of stock - distribution and stock status

STOCK-OUT IS THE AVAILABILITY ANSWER, not the form's stock_classification field. That field was computed before the availability correction and labels only 643 rows a stock out where 816 medicines were in fact not on the shelf. EVERY STOCK-OUT IS COUNTED, whatever the consumption figure: a medicine out for the whole window often records zero consumption because it was never there to dispense, so excluding those rows would drop the longest stock-outs and understate the rate. The AMC = 0 exclusion applies only to the 1,154 rows that were ON THE SHELF with no recorded consumption, where months of stock cannot be computed and the medicine was present anyway. The four categories are mutually exclusive and sum to the base.

2.2-2.4Inventory record accuracy

DENOMINATOR CORRECTION: the prompt implies all assessed observations, but physical and recorded counts exist only where the medicine is available. The base is 8,873 available rows, not 9,870 managed rows. EXCLUSION: every record that does not name a digital recording system is dropped - 181 rows - because where no system was named there is no digital record for a physical count to be checked against. The field is never literally blank on this base; it holds 'none', 'N/A', a bare number or an unrelated remark instead. The rows come from 43 facilities, of which 6 named no system anywhere in their basket: Gasenga HP, IKIZERE-MUREHE HP, KAMUHOZA HP, KIBERINKA - GAHONDO HP, Kinoni CS, Mahaza HP. All of them remain in every other indicator.

3.3Consumption variability by therapeutic class

CV = standard deviation of the three monthly values / their mean x 100. It is undefined where a pair consumed nothing at all, so the base is 8,336 of 9,870 complete pairs. A high share erratic means demand at that class cannot be planned from a three-month average, which is what AMC-based ordering assumes.

Analysis 4 · Stock-out frequency and duration

FIG 4.1Stock-out incidence by level of care

How it is calculated: Managed rows with at least one stock-out day, Jun-Aug / all managed rows, by level of care.

Share of managed facility x medicine pairs with at least one stock-out day in the window. A longer bar is worse.

FIG 4.2Stock-out incidence by drug class

How it is calculated: Managed rows with at least one stock-out day, Jun-Aug / all managed rows, by drug class.

Highest incidence first. Classes with fewer than 30 managed pairs are left out. A longer bar is worse.

FIG 4.3Stock-out incidence by programme

How it is calculated: Managed rows with at least one stock-out day, Jun-Aug / all managed rows, by programme.

Highest incidence first. A longer bar is worse.

FIG 4.4Average stock-out days by drug class

How it is calculated: Stock-out days June + July + August, summed per managed pair; mean over the pairs with at least one day out, by drug class.

Mean days out per affected pair, longest first. Classes with fewer than 30 affected pairs are left out. The track is the 92-day window.

FIG 4.5Average stock-out days by programme

How it is calculated: Stock-out days June + July + August, summed per managed pair; mean over the pairs with at least one day out, by programme.

Mean days out per affected pair, longest first. The track is the 92-day window.

4.7Every medicine assessed, by stock-out burden

All 79 medicines in the basket, each against its own denominator, worst incidence first. INCIDENCE is the share of managed pairs out at least one day in June-August. DAYS POSSIBLE is managed pairs x 92 days - every day each pair could have been out - and DAYS OUT RATE is total days out over it. AVERAGE DAYS OUT is total days out over the pairs ever out, the same measure as FIG 4.4-4.5. Incidence and duration rank medicines differently - out briefly but often is not the same problem as out for months - so both are shown. Days are summed from the three monthly fields, not from the form's total_stockout_days, which adds the ongoing current run and exceeds the 92-day window on 355 rows. Full crosstabs by level, province, district and management type are in Stockout_analysis.xlsx.

How these figures are calculated

Every value on this page is read from the same row sets the indicators use, so it cannot drift from the figures it explains. Only the definitions and the reasons are written by hand.

METHOD1. What one row is

MeasureHow it is calculatedValue
Stock assessment, sheet 2one row per facility x medicine assessed14,398
Facilities visiteddistinct facility names in the submissions267
Moleculesmedicines after strengths of one molecule are collapsed (Method 3)71
Items before collapsingmedicines as the form lists them81

METHOD2. Cleaning applied before counting

MeasureHow it is calculatedValue
S2 duplicate rows removedsame facility x medicine recorded twice; the row with more fields filled is kept12
S6 EML applicability correctedform said No where the official EML list holds the medicine at that level of care -> Yes608
S6 not changed (opposite direction)form says Yes where the list does not hold it at that level - reported, left as recorded82
S7 availability correctedanswered 'available = Yes' with 0 units on the shelf -> No173
S8 recording system names normalisedfree text; one spelling per system, bare numbers removed6905

METHOD3. Method 3 - combining strengths

MeasureHow it is calculatedValue
The ruleper facility: a molecule is MANAGED if any strength is managed, and AVAILABLE if any managed strength was on the shelf
Whytwo strengths are interchangeable - a facility holding Metformin 500mg can treat a patient needing metformin
What does NOT collapsequantities, months of stock, stock-out days, requisitions and financial loss stay at item level - summing 500mg and 850mg tablets gives a meaningless number

METHOD4. The availability denominator

MeasureHow it is calculatedValue
EXPECTED (the denominator)set by medicine_program - two tracks, below9,782
Essential Medicines trackevery molecule the EML authorises at that facility's level of care, managed or not5,235
Programme track (Malaria, MCCH, FP, ARV, TB, Consumables)only the molecules the facility manages - programme products are allocated, so not holding one is not a shortage4,547
of which MANAGEDthe facility actually stocks it9,016
of which NOT managed (Essential Medicines only)authorised but the facility does not stock it - counted UNAVAILABLE under the study definition766
AVAILABLE (the numerator)managed AND on the shelf on the visit day8,381
Managed but emptystocked, but nothing on the shelf635
OVERALL AVAILABILITYAVAILABLE / EXPECTED85.68%
Memo: over managed rows onlyAVAILABLE / MANAGED - the figure if a medicine the facility chooses not to stock is left out92.96%

METHOD5. Other denominators

MeasureHow it is calculatedValue
Inventory accuracyphysical count = system count, over AVAILABLE rows only - a count exists only where there is stock; facilities that named no digital system are excluded8,873
Stock-out incidencepairs with at least one stock-out day June-August, over MANAGED pairs9,870
Stock-out dayssummed from the three monthly fields, NOT the form's total_stockout_days, which adds the ongoing current run and exceeds the 92-day window on 355 rows
Order fill ratequantity delivered / quantity requested, Jun-Aug, over the medicine-months where requested >= delivered (over-deliveries dropped)216 months dropped
CHW availabilityavailable / (managed and answered); 'not managed' is MFT zoning, not a stock-out, so it stays out of the denominator1,180
Prescription fulfilmentitems recorded available / items with an answer - a design artefact of who gets recorded; compare groups, not the level14,059

METHOD6. Suppression

MeasureHow it is calculatedValue
Minimum 30 observationsa rate computed on fewer is left blank rather than ranked; the counts are still shown
Minimum 10 per facilityfor the facility dots in FIG 4 - a facility basket of 16 medicines is a usable rate, 30 would drop 15 of 26 health posts
